```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

Define a protocol before scoring. Values must already use the declared units.
The following example uses synthetic measurements, not clinical thresholds.

```{r}
library(allostaticR)
data <- simulate_biomarkers(100)
spec <- define_protocol(list(
  define_biomarker("sbp", "cardiovascular", "high", "mmHg"),
  define_biomarker("hdl", "metabolic", "low", "mg/dL"),
  define_biomarker("crp", "inflammatory", "high", "mg/L")
))
reference <- fit_reference(data, spec, label = "Synthetic baseline")
reference_cutoffs(reference)
result <- allostatic_load(data, reference = reference, id = "id", group = "group", graphics = "auto")
summary(result)
result$plots$distribution
result$plots$biomarkers
result$plots$coverage
result$plots$groups
```

Thresholds are fixed after fitting. Applying them to new data never re-estimates
the reference quantiles. High risk uses the upper quantile; low risk uses its
complement. Equality counts as risk unless `inclusive = FALSE`. Ties can produce
risk prevalences above the nominal tail probability. Bilateral risk uses both tails.

```{r}
new_data <- simulate_biomarkers(20, seed = 7)
new_result <- score_load(new_data, reference, id = "id")
head(as.data.frame(new_result, what = "components"))
```

Missing observations remain missing contributions. Complete panels are required
by default. An alternative protocol can explicitly choose a proportion score and
minimum coverage. Scores on different scales should not share a classification
threshold. System summaries show observed proportions, not additional score terms.

For publication, obtain English labels and customize the ggplot objects:

```{r}
plot_load(result, "distribution", locale = "en") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Synthetic cohort")
```

Save any customized graphic with `ggplot2::ggsave()`. There are no automatic
significance tests or clinical risk categories.


## Define your own graphic

Scoring returns data without creating figures by default. Choose your own
geometry, axes, scales, colors and theme with standard ggplot2 functions:

```{r custom-graphic}
scores <- plot_data(result, "scores")
ggplot2::ggplot(scores, ggplot2::aes(x = group, y = score)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(fill = "white", width = 0.55, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Study group", y = "Allostatic load score") +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

Use `type = "biomarkers"` for long-format measured values, `"systems"` for
system risk proportions, or `"cutoffs"` for fixed reference thresholds.
Missing values remain in the extracted data. Presets from `plot_load()` are
editable ggplot objects; pass `graphics = "auto"` to `allostatic_load()` to
build the full preset collection.
